summary: The Atto 2 is BYD's smallest SUV in Australia and, from $31,990 before on-road costs, the cheapest electric SUV on sale here — a point almost every local reviewer leads with. Testers consistently find it comfortable, quiet and easy to live with, and note real-world efficiency that beats the claim, but they are equally consistent that its 51.13kWh battery and 82kW DC charging peak make it a city and suburbs car rather than a country-trip one. Opinion splits on whether the soft, light-steering setup reads as relaxed or as vague, and the missing ANCAP rating is the recurring reservation.
pros: Cheapest electric SUV in Australia at $31,990 before on-road costs, undercutting the Chery E5 and Jaecoo J5 EV by roughly $4,000-$5,000 in Dynamic form
Real-world efficiency beats the 17.1kWh/100km claim — CarExpert recorded 13.7, Chasing Cars 14.2 and RACV 12-13.9kWh/100km, so the 345km WLTP figure holds up in suburban use
Both grades get the full active-safety set as standard, including AEB with pedestrian and cyclist detection, blind-spot monitoring, rear cross-traffic alert and adaptive cruise
Six-year/150,000km vehicle warranty is unconditional — no dealer-servicing strings — plus eight years/160,000km on the Blade battery
Premium's $4,000 walk-up is unusually well filled: 12.8-inch rotating screen, panoramic roof, 360-degree camera, heated and ventilated power driver's seat and eight speakers
cons: No ANCAP rating at all, and BYD has no plans to have it locally tested; reviewers note it lacks a driver monitoring system, which rules out five stars under current criteria
82kW DC charging peak means roughly 38-40 minutes for 10-80 per cent — slow enough that CarsGuide, CarExpert and Chasing Cars all flag it as the car's main road-trip limitation
Australia gets only the 51.13kWh battery; the 64.8kWh long-range version sold in Europe is not offered here, so 345km WLTP is the ceiling
No spare wheel on either grade — CarsGuide called this "unacceptable in Australia"
Soft suspension and very light, low-feedback steering leave it wallowy at speed, and several testers had to repeatedly switch off oversensitive lane-keeping and speed alerts
